clue.text: All in large unwieldy guide

parts.note: large means fat, as of a big body

indicators.note: something unwieldy is awkward and out of shape, so the letters of guide are rearranged

explanation.surface: A big, cumbersome guidebook that nobody can easily carry around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwieldy' rearranges GUIDE into IGUED, which follows FAT.
explanation.definitionFit: All in is informal British for utterly exhausted, the same as tired out.

clue.text: The elements increase for 7's granny

parts.note: the elements are wind, rain and so on, the weather
to wax is to grow, as the moon does

explanation.surface: Somebody's grandmother grows ever more exposed to wind and rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is the author answer at 7 Down; his Discworld novels feature the witch known as Granny of this surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Esme, called Granny, is the senior witch in Terry Pratchett's Discworld stories.

clue.text: Time to interrupt the last word in dance music of the 1990s

indicators.note: in places the rest inside the dance word

parts.note: a bop is an informal dance

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so T goes inside RIP

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the final word on a gravestone

explanation.surface: A clock cutting off the final say in a nightclub track from the nineties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to interrupt' puts T inside RIP to make RITP, and 'in' sets that inside BOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Britpop was the guitar-band genre of mid-1990s Britain, with groups such as Oasis and Blur.

clue.text: Top speed restricting the Queen, king becoming ruler

indicators.note: restricting means holding within, so the queen's letters go inside
to top something is to cut its head off, so the first letter of the speed word goes

parts.note: tempo is musical speed
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's cipher
R, rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A top speed limit placed on the monarch, with the king turning into a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' removes the first letter of TEMPO to leave EMPO; 'restricting' places ER inside it, giving EMPERO, then R follows. 'becoming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the sovereign of an empire, a supreme monarch.

clue.text: Problem getting round for the big event?

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Trouble arising as things go full circle before a major occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: the wrestlers in this sport are famously huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is Japanese wrestling contested by very heavy men, so it is literally an event for the big.

clue.text: Energy from Galician city overcoming old Iraqi city

indicators.note: in a down clue, overcoming means sitting on top of, so the Spanish city comes first

parts.note: Vigo is a port city in Galicia, north-west Spain
Ur was an ancient Sumerian city in what is now Iraq

explanation.surface: A Spanish city defeating an ancient Mesopotamian one, a source of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigour is physical strength and vitality, much like energy.

clue.text: Author's material, exercise involving unidirectional device

parts.note: terry is a looped cotton fabric used for towels

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so the exercise letters enclose the device

parts.note: PT is physical training
a ratchet lets a wheel or bar turn one way only

explanation.surface: A writer's fabric, and a workout using a one-way mechanism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts RATCHET between P and T. The 's in the definition reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Terry Pratchett was the English novelist who wrote the Discworld series.

clue.text: Lay a sexual partner, pure at heart

parts.note: a mate is an animal's sexual partner

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so the central letters of pure are taken

explanation.surface: A purely innocent lover in bed, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like a verb with a sexual sense; it is the adjective meaning non-professional.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay as an adjective means non-specialist, as in a lay reader: someone not professionally trained.

clue.text: See 14
See 14 Down
General meaning to make a pile in winter

definitions.meaning: the ... of an argument is its general gist
snow ... when the wind heaps it into banks

explanation.definitionFit: Drift is both the gist of what is said and, as a verb, to be blown into heaps, as snow is.

clue.text: Chocolate or gum, if chewed, 7's work

indicators.note: chewed means mangled in the mouth, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sweets or gum chomped on, apparently a writer's output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewed' rearranges all sixteen letters of CHOCOLATE OR GUM IF; the answer runs on into 23 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colour of Magic (1983) is the first Discworld novel by Terry Pratchett, the 7 Down author.

clue.text: I head-butt 'eart-throb where baby's kept safe?

parts.note: to nut someone is British slang for head-butting them
heart-throb is a hero; dropping its H, as the apostrophe in 'eart shows, leaves ERO

explanation.surface: A Cockney fan lunging headfirst at a pin-up idol.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'eart signals a dropped H, so the same is done to HERO.
explanation.definitionFit: In utero is Latin for inside the womb, where an unborn child is protected.

clue.text: Rocky formation cut with poor rocks

indicators.note: rocks means shakes about, so the letters of cut and poor are jumbled

explanation.surface: Geology about a stone formation hewn among inferior stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like part of the geology; it is the anagram signal, and 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is a part of the bedrock showing at the surface of the ground.

clue.text: 7's work heeded, in truth, with a dozen amusing academic rats, possibly?

indicators.note: possibly means these letters might be arranged another way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scholar listens earnestly to twelve comic laboratory rats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges thirty-eight letters, from HEEDED IN TRUTH and A DOZEN AMUSING ACADEMIC RATS; 'with' is a link. The answer runs through 9 Across, 8 Down and 20 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazing Maurice and his Educated Rodents (2001) is a Discworld novel for younger readers by Terry Pratchett.

clue.text: Sixth wife, not the fourth, as average

indicators.note: the fourth letter of the surname is left out

parts.note: Catherine Parr was the sixth wife of Henry VIII

explanation.surface: Henry VIII's last queen, minus a letter, reckoned middling.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the normal or typical level, as in 'below par'.

clue.text: Funds to stop the pain?

parts.note: to end is to stop
ow is a cry of pain, and several such cries are ows

explanation.surface: Money to make an ache go away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funds' is a verb here: to endow is to provide money for. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow an institution is to give it a permanent income, financing it.

clue.text: Raise hell about British nation

indicators.note: about means around, so the anagram goes round the British letter
hell suggests chaos, so the letters of raise are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A call to cause chaos around a British country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hell' rearranges RAISE into SERIA, and 'about' puts it round B.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbia is a Balkan country, capital Belgrade.

clue.text: Musician, say, brought up to suck seed in pub

indicators.note: in puts all of that inside the pub word

parts.note: a bar is a drinking place

indicators.note: to suck something in is to take it inside, so the reversed letters hold the seed
in a down clue, brought up means lifted from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is often clued by say
a pip is a fruit seed

explanation.surface: A musician raised to draw on a seed while sitting in a tavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is not part of the definition: it is EG, which 'brought up' turns to GE. 'to suck' puts PIP inside, giving GPIPE, and 'in' sets that inside BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagpiper is a performer who plays the bagpipes.

clue.text: Atmospheric tune?

parts.note: the clue reads as a moody melody, but combines the stuff of the atmosphere with a word for a melody, both one word

explanation.definitionFit: Air is both the gas mixture we breathe and a simple song or melody.

clue.text: Put off by a jacket with our name

parts.note: a DJ is a dinner jacket
taken as written

explanation.surface: Delayed by a formal jacket bearing our name tag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjourn a meeting is to postpone it to a later date.

clue.text: See 14
Mad nut sacked, so escaping duty

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters of nut are muddled

parts.note: to be axed is to be sacked from a job

explanation.surface: A crazy man fired, so he avoids paying tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' rearranges NUT into UNT; 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are untaxed are free of any levy, so no tax is owed on them.

clue.text: Bird on top of man whistling, raised hat

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top of means placed above, so the bird comes first

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: a ref, or referee, blows the whistle in a match

explanation.surface: A bird perched on a whistling man, who lifts his hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns REF into FER. TITFER is old British rhyming slang (tit for tat, hat).
explanation.definitionFit: Titfer is Cockney rhyming slang for headgear, from tit for tat.

clue.text: See 11
Vegetable I struggle to eat, requiring skill as a starter?

indicators.note: as a starter means coming first, so the skill word leads

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation
taken as written
to choke is to struggle when swallowing food

explanation.surface: Someone choking on a vegetable that takes skill to eat as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a starter' looks like a menu course; it places ART at the front. 'requiring' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is a thistle-like plant whose flower head is eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Bath perhaps filling Atlantic, it yields

indicators.note: filling means sitting inside, so the answer lies within these words

explanation.surface: A spa town flooding the ocean as it gives way.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath, a spa city in south-west England, is given as an example, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath has city status in England, so it is one example of a large town.

clue.text: Old country's river passing two sharp bends?

indicators.note: passing means going past, so the river follows the bends

parts.note: the letter Z is drawn with two sharp turns, like a road sign for bends
the Aire is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A former nation's river winding past two tight corners.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is'. Zaire was the name of the Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1971 to 1997.
explanation.definitionFit: Zaire is a former name for the central African state now called the DR Congo.

clue.text: Horse still ahead of tailless bird

indicators.note: ahead of means placed before, so this word comes first

parts.note: still and even are both used to intensify, as in still better, even better

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A horse remains in front of a bird missing its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' cuts the last letter from TERN to leave TER.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a horse trained for eventing, which combines dressage, cross-country and show jumping.

clue.text: Film director Lee's intent, to provide touching line

indicators.note: the first two letters of intent signal placing inside

parts.note: the rest of intent is a tent
Ang Lee is the Taiwanese film director of Life of Pi

explanation.surface: A film-maker's purpose, to supply a line on the touchline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intent' splits as IN TENT: ANG goes inside TENT. 'to provide' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangent in geometry is a straight line meeting a curve at one point without crossing it.
